blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A board scenario forces P030 in, and P030 clashes with its alternative P031, which another override forces in. Why does the steps/07 conflict name in_P030?

options.text: The scenario edits the export so that P030 becomes a must-do
options.says: A scenario never edits the export; apply makes a new Request.

options.text: The override is a bound on P030's variables, which the filter reads
options.says: The deletion filter relaxes only rows; a bound could not be named.

options.text: The override is a named row, and the filter relaxes named rows
options.says: Right: that is why the planner writes overrides as rows.

options.text: The filter skips the export's rules and reports only overrides
options.says: The conflict on the page also names alt_G030, a rule from the export.

origin.section: A Scenario Is Data Beside the Export, and an Override Is a Named Row

questions.stem: Someone edits a stored snapshot's body directly in the SQLite file. What happens the next time the store reads that snapshot?

options.text: It refuses it, since the body no longer matches its hash
options.says: Right: snapshot() recomputes the hash and raises when it differs.

options.text: It returns the edit, since the file is the record of truth
options.says: The hash is the record of truth; a body that does not match is refused.

options.text: It stores the edit again under the hash of the new body
options.says: Reading never writes; the read raises a ValueError.

options.text: It returns the body and adds a warning row to the run table
options.says: The read raises; nothing is returned and nothing is written.

origin.section: Tests Check the Store by Its Contract, Not Its Tables

questions.stem: Why does the store keep the export exactly as received rather than the Request the loader built from it?

options.text: So a loader fix rewrites old snapshots to match the new code
options.says: A loader fix changes the Request, never the stored snapshot.

options.text: So a replay can skip the loader and plan from stored records
options.says: A replay runs the new loader on the old bytes.

options.text: So scenarios can edit the stored export before each run
options.says: A scenario never edits the export.

options.text: So an old run can be replayed on the same bytes with new code
options.says: Right: storing the Request would freeze a loader bug into every record.

origin.section: Design Note: The Snapshot Is the Unit of Truth
